components.title: Model endpoints
components.description: Configured local and remote model providers.

control-implementations.description: Provider-bound safeguards, and the model approvals each request is checked against.

implemented-requirements.description: Configured private endpoints are checked before confidential requests are sent.

statements.description: The extension checks a configured private endpoint's connection binding before it sends Confidential content. A mismatch refuses the request instead of falling back to an unpinned connection.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects providers and decides whether their service assurances are sufficient.

implemented-requirements.description: The crypto inventory records listed algorithms and separately records X25519 and scrypt use.

statements.description: The crypto inventory records the listed algorithms used by the product and the collector reports their documented standing.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects and approves cryptographic use in its deployment.

statements.description: The inventory records X25519 and scrypt separately, so an unfavorable standing prevents this component from presenting complete cryptographic coverage.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides whether algorithms outside the referenced list are acceptable.

implemented-requirements.description: Model licences recorded per model and checked at the publisher.

statements.description: Each model approval SovAI ships records the licence its publisher states, read at the publisher's page, and the fit register (compliance/resources.json) holds one model entry per shipped approval with that licence and the conditions of its use. Command A+ is approved only on the Cohere Model Vault classes; your organization's own on-premise copy needs your organization's approval with the artifact hash. A licence the model's service reports that differs from the approval's ends the approval until your organization signs a new one.
statements.remarks: Your organization approves its own models in its signed rules and decides whether a publisher's licence terms suit its use.

props.name: limitation
props.value: How NEAR AI passes the publishers' licence terms through to your organization is not answered (G412).

implemented-requirements.description: Where each model may run, as its approval says.

statements.description: Each model approval lists the places it may run, in the Runs on classes, and under enforce a request to any other place is refused before anything is sent. When the place behind an approved model changes from the first one seen, the approval ends until your organization signs a new one. SovAI's shipped approvals never place Command A+ on NEAR AI's private hardware.
statements.remarks: Your organization chooses its AI services and holds their service agreements.

implemented-requirements.description: Model licences that allow research only.

statements.description: A model whose licence is on SovAI's fixed list of non-commercial licences is used for research only, except through the vendor's own service (a Cohere vault class), where the vendor's commercial terms apply. A refusal names the licence.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets each approval's uses in its signed rules, which is where any other licence restriction is applied.

implemented-requirements.description: The origin rule, from your organization's signed rules.

statements.description: Model approvals come from your organization's signed rules, or from the shipped approvals when it has none. A model whose developer is in the People's Republic of China is approved for research only, in the research workspace, which cannot open project files, run commands or use tools. Under enforce any other use of it is refused before anything is sent, and chat you review needs an exception that your organization's rules carry; an exception signed only on this computer covers nothing.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which models it approves, and sets its rules to enforce.

props.name: limitation
props.value: Until your organization's rules enforce, approvals are only reported, and today's models, including those from the People's Republic of China, keep doing agent work (G409). The research workspace is kept apart by SovAI's own checks, not by the operating system (G413).

implemented-requirements.description: Lineage, provenance on outputs and the AI bill of materials.

statements.description: Each approval records the model's lineage: developer, origin, family, base model and teachers, and, for your organization's own hosting, the artifact hash. Every model request's record names the use, the approval by id and hash, and any refusal reason. Export AI Bill of Materials writes a CycloneDX 1.6 bill for a project with one entry per model it used: supplier, licence, artifact hash when known, base and teachers with their origin, approval hash, place class and uses served.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the bill with its project records and passes it to whoever assesses the work.

props.name: limitation
props.value: On NEAR AI's private hardware an approval binds to the model id, not to the exact model files, because the attestation does not report the files' hash (G411).

implemented-requirements.description: Your organization's evaluation before any role, and checks by another model family.

statements.description: Under enforce, a model takes any use above research, checking roles included, only when its approval cites your organization's evaluation of those model files and covers the use. The one exception is chat you review allowed by an exception your organization's rules carry.
statements.remarks: Your organization evaluates and red-teams each model before it approves it for a role.

props.name: limitation
props.value: The shipped approvals carry no evaluation, so under enforce nothing goes above research until your organization evaluates its models (G410). An exception records its mission benefit, not a reference to your organization's assessment (G537).

statements.description: Every checking role (the safety classifier, reviewers, plan checkers, verifiers, editors, red team, the staff release guard and the J2 tradecraft reviewer) runs on a model of another family than the model whose work it checks, taken from the approval's lineage; when none is allowed, a person decides, and the record names both families.
statements.remarks: Your organization approves models of more than one family, so checks can run.

implemented-requirements.description: Every shipped model in the fit register, every used model in the AI bill of materials.

statements.description: Every model approval SovAI ships has an entry of kind model in the fit register, and the register check fails when a shipped approval has no entry or an entry names a model nothing ships. Every model a project used is listed in its AI bill of materials, from this computer's model-request log.
statements.remarks: Your organization adds the models it approves itself to its own inventory.
